chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Hassan ibn Mihran who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Mecca is the sanctuary of Allah, and Medina is the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Kufa is my sanctuary. A tyrant who transgresses in it, Allah will break him.'

key_terms.حَرَمُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Kufa as the sanctuary of Imam Ali according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates a tripartite hierarchy of sacred spaces, elevating Kufa to the status of Imam Ali’s personal sanctuary (*Haram*), distinct from the universal sanctity of Mecca and the prophetic sanctity of Medina. It underscores the political-theological concept of divine retribution against tyrannical rulers (*Jabbar*) who violate the rights and justice associated with the Imam’s domain, reflecting the Shia emphasis on Kufa as a center of authority and resistance.
